title: Symmetry and Parity of the Rational Function g(x) = x / (x^2 - 1)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Test the function g(x) = x / (x^2 - 1) algebraically for even and odd symmetry, and justify your answer.

steps.title: Substitute -x into the Formula
steps.explanation: Replace every occurrence of x in the rational formula with -x on the symmetric domain x != +/-1.
steps.why: Testing for function parity begins by computing the output for the negated input -x.

steps.title: Simplify the Denominator
steps.explanation: Because squaring a negative number yields a positive result, (-x)^2 = x^2, leaving the denominator unchanged while the numerator is negated.
steps.why: Even powers of real numbers are invariant under negation: (-x)^2 = x^2.

steps.title: Compare with -g(x) and Conclude
steps.explanation: Factoring the minus sign in front of the fraction establishes that g(-x) = -g(x) for all x != +/-1, so g is an odd function.
steps.why: The quotient of an odd function (numerator x) and an even function (denominator x^2 - 1) is an odd function.
